request.spec:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every change to a sheet now writes one line to the audit file, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**Front end:** the server had no way to know who was signed in, so adding or editing a person or a claim now sends the signed-in user as `?user=<name>` (in `features/people/People.tsx` and `features/claims/Claims.tsx`).

**Server:** I added a separate audit step to each of the four endpoints. It runs after the change is stored, just before the response is sent:
- `AuditPersonAdded` writes `PERSON_ADDED sheet=… by=… name=… grade=…`
- `AuditPersonEdited` writes `PERSON_EDITED` with the same fields.
- `AuditClaimAdded` writes `CLAIM_ADDED sheet=… by=… person=… amount=… date=…`
- `AuditClaimEdited` writes `CLAIM_EDITED` with the same fields. It looks up the claim's person to get the name.

Amounts are written with two decimals, the same as the screen, and dates as yyyy-mm-dd.

**Refused changes:** the audit step is the last step before the response, so a change refused by any rule stops earlier and writes no line. That includes rules added later, as long as they are placed before the audit step.

**Things to know:**
- The audit line is written just before the database commits. If a commit failed at that point, the line would already be written even though nothing was saved.
- The user is optional on the server. A request sent without it would be recorded as `by=null` instead of being refused.
